name: Military Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1775) (C0033)

techniques.comment: The issuing of Catherine II's August manifesto, officially erasing the very memory of the Sich: it was destroyed "with the extirpation for the future of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks," for the empire resolved "to destroy the Zaporozhian Sich and the name of the Cossacks derived from it"(Citation: Манифест об уничтожении Запорожской Сечи 1775). Hrushevsky: "The Sich was destroyed, and on 3 August a tsarist decree announced its abolition, 'with the annihilation of the very name of the Zaporozhian Cossacks'"(Citation: Ілюстрована історія України 1921).

The encirclement and forcible seizure of the Sich by imperial troops right after the Cossacks had helped the empire win the war. The manifesto records the operation matter-of-factly: "On June 4, Our Lieutenant-General Tekeli, with the troops entrusted to him by us, occupied the Zaporozhian Sich"(Citation: Манифест об уничтожении Запорожской Сечи 1775).

The arrest and exile of the Sich's top leadership: "In July 1775, after the destruction of the New Sich, by order of Empress Catherine II, Kalnyshevsky was arrested and sent to the prison of the Solovetsky monastery"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 4 2007). Kalnyshevsky spent more than 25 years in confinement; formally freed in 1801, he died in the monastery.
